# PatchLabs: full description for language models

Last updated 10 November 2026 (v3). Short index: https://patchlabs.dev/llms.txt

## What PatchLabs is

PatchLabs is a security platform for apps built with AI tools such as Lovable, Supabase, Bolt, Replit and Cursor, in four product lines (Lab, Code, Fix, Watch; see below). It finds personal-data leaks, exposed keys and risky AI-written code, and proves database fixes before anyone ships them. Positioning: "Find the leak. Prove the fix." Lab-proven fixes for apps built with AI.

A scanner gives you a list of findings. PatchLabs gives you a fix you have watched work: every fix is tested in a lab against three identities.

PatchLabs is independent. It is not affiliated with Lovable, Supabase, Bolt, Replit or Cursor; it works with apps built on them.

## How a check works

1. You paste a public GitHub repo URL and your email at https://patchlabs.dev/#check.
2. You prove you own the repo by committing `patchlabs-verify.txt` containing a one-time code to the default branch (a one-click GitHub link fills it in).
3. A worker clones the repo and removes repo-supplied agent configuration (`.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`).
4. It rebuilds the database from the repo's `supabase/migrations` in a disposable local Postgres that copies Supabase's roles, auth functions and default grants, and seeds fake test rows.
5. It tests what three identities can read on every table holding personal data (email, phone, address, date of birth and similar): an anonymous visitor (the anon role your public key maps to), a signed-in stranger, and the owner.
6. PatchLabs Code scans the code and the full git history for exposed AI, payment and database keys (values are masked), and reads the repo for the code findings listed below, including npm dependency versions checked against OSV.
7. If something leaks, a fix agent writes a SQL migration (plus any code change it notes). The smallest Claude model goes first; a larger one is tried only if the lab proof fails, within a spend cap per check. The agent has no web access, can edit only the fix folder and the working copy, and can run only the lab verifier.
8. An independent verifier rebuilds a fresh lab with the fix applied and re-tests: anonymous visitor denied, stranger denied, owner still reads their own rows. If that fails on every model, a person reviews it.
9. The lab database is dropped. You get a report page with the fix as a downloadable migration and a one-click "commit this file on GitHub" link, plus a signed receipt.

A check never connects to the customer's live app or database. PatchLabs never asks for a database password and never pushes to the customer's repo. PatchLabs never touches your database. Live posture only loads your public home page, like any visitor, and only on domains you verify. The owner's engineer approves every change.

What is not available yet (say so honestly): private repos and automatic pull requests need a GitHub App, which is coming. Card payments are not live; paid plans are by request.

## Real numbers (PatchLabs lab study, November 2026)

- 436 public Lovable/Supabase repos run (from a random sample of 500); in 318 the migrations built a working database in the lab.
- 106 of 318 (33%) let the wrong people read personal data: 70 (22%) to anyone on the internet with the public key, 36 more (11%) to anyone who signs up. After removing businesses' own public contact details, the rate is about 1 in 4 (25-28%).
- Fix agents, re-verified: 19 of 20 real fixes worked first time and applied cleanly (5 Nov 2026, n=20).
- Autonomous pipeline on 20 new apps (9 Nov 2026, n=20): 18 of 20 fixes passed the strict lab proof with no human; 15 needed only the smallest model; median 3.5 minutes per app; the other 2 went to a person.
- The study is published as aggregate counts only. No app from the study is named.

## Product lines (v3, 10 Nov 2026)

- PatchLabs Lab (https://patchlabs.dev/product/lab): rebuilds the database from the repo's migrations in a disposable Postgres and reproduces each leak as an anonymous visitor, a signed-in stranger and the owner. Findings are marked proven.
- PatchLabs Code (https://patchlabs.dev/product/code): reads the repo without running its code or installing packages: keys in the current code and full git history, Supabase Edge Functions and supabase/config.toml, payment webhooks (Stripe, Lemon Squeezy, Paddle), CORS headers, browser-only admin checks, roles read from user_metadata, raw HTML rendering, Firebase rules files, and npm dependency versions from lockfiles checked against the OSV database (only package names and versions are sent to OSV; reported as skipped when offline). Findings carry a file and line and are not lab-proven.
- PatchLabs Fix (https://patchlabs.dev/product/fix): writes the migration, proves it in a fresh lab as the three identities, asks the owner's business questions, and waits for the engineer to approve. One-click commit on GitHub, MCP and CI. Automatic pull requests: coming with the GitHub App.
- PatchLabs Watch (https://patchlabs.dev/product/watch): scheduled re-checks, diffs, alerts, badge, signed receipts, public proof page, teams.
- Live posture (https://patchlabs.dev/product/live-posture), part of Watch and opt-in per app: for a domain the team verifies (a file at /patchlabs-verify.txt or a patchlabs-verify meta tag), PatchLabs loads the public home page the way any visitor's browser does: one plain http:// request to see if it redirects, one https:// page load following at most 5 redirects, and that load's TLS handshake. It grades HTTPS, the certificate, security headers, cookie flags and mixed content (A to F; score 100 minus 30 per high, 15 per medium, 5 per low finding; an invalid or expired certificate is always F), re-checks daily, alerts by email and webhook when the grade drops or a finding appears, and offers a live badge. No other paths, no forms, no API calls, no database, no attack payloads. It does not test the app for data leaks or vulnerabilities.

## Finding format

Every finding: {"id": "PL-001", "line": "lab|code|live", "severity": "critical|high|medium|low|info", "title", "object", "file", "line_no", "evidence" (short, redacted), "proven" (true only when the lab reproduced it), "proof", "fix" (one line), "fixed_in_lab", "advisory" (PL-023 only)}. A finished check's API summary carries "findings" (up to 200) and "counts" by severity. Docs: https://patchlabs.dev/docs/findings

## Finding IDs

Live, Lab: PL-001 anonymous visitor can read personal data; PL-002 any signed-in user can read every row; PL-003 rLS enabled but no policies (owner locked out); PL-004 uPDATE policy missing WITH CHECK; PL-005 always-true policy; PL-006 sECURITY DEFINER function exposed; PL-007 public storage bucket; PL-008 row level security not enabled.
Live, Code: PL-009 aI, payment or database key in the code; PL-010 service role key in client code; PL-011 key still in git history; PL-017 edge function open without sign-in while using the service key; PL-018 sign-ups need no email confirmation; PL-019 access decided by user_metadata, which users can edit; PL-020 admin check only in the browser; PL-021 payment webhook doesn't verify its signature; PL-022 edge function trusts a user id sent in the request; PL-023 dependency with a known vulnerability; PL-024 user content rendered as raw HTML; PL-025 firebase rules allow anyone; PL-026 any website can call a signed-in function.
Live, Live posture (opt-in, verified domain): PL-027 site doesn't force HTTPS; PL-028 TLS certificate is invalid, expired or expires within 21 days; PL-029 no HSTS header, or max-age under 180 days; PL-030 no Content-Security-Policy; PL-031 any site can frame the page; PL-032 no X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; PL-033 cookie set without Secure, or a session cookie without HttpOnly; PL-034 page loads scripts or styles over plain HTTP; PL-035 server headers reveal software versions; PL-036 no Referrer-Policy.
Coming (documented, not tested yet, never in reports): PL-012 strangers can change or delete other people's rows; PL-013 users can make themselves admin; PL-014 view skips row level security; PL-015 stored files readable or writable by anyone; PL-016 realtime sends private rows to subscribers.
Each ID has a page at https://patchlabs.dev/findings/pl-0NN with vulnerable example code, a self-check, the fix and why it is rated as it is. Index with filters: https://patchlabs.dev/findings

## Plans (limits enforced by the API)

- Free: £0. 1 app, monthly re-check, 4 manual runs per month, 1 seat.
- Maker: £19/month. 3 apps, weekly or monthly re-checks, 30 manual runs per month, 2 seats.
- Agency: £99/month for 10 apps, +£8 per extra app. Weekly or monthly, 200 manual runs per month, 10 seats.
- Enterprise: custom.
API keys, webhooks, badges and client labels are on every plan. Upgrades: request in the app; we reply within a day.

## Product surfaces

- Free check (no account): https://patchlabs.dev/#check, report at /check?id=<id>.
- Signed-in app (passwordless email link): dashboard of monitored apps, scheduled re-checks, diff since the last check, approve or reject findings, answer the report's business questions, team invites, API keys, webhooks (Slack-compatible), data export and account deletion. https://patchlabs.dev/app/
- Public badge: https://api.patchlabs.dev/badge/<app id>.svg shows "no known leaks", "fix in progress", "not checked yet" or "private", with the last check date.
- Public proof page: https://patchlabs.dev/proof?app=<app id> (only when the owner makes it public).
- Free RLS check (static analysis, no sign-up): https://patchlabs.dev/tools/rls-check
- Free security headers check (no sign-up, one public page load, result not stored, 10 an hour per network): https://patchlabs.dev/tools/headers-check
- REST API: https://api.patchlabs.dev. Errors are {"detail": "human sentence"}. Signed-in calls: Authorization: Bearer <session>. CI calls: X-API-Key: pl_live_... Docs: https://patchlabs.dev/docs/api
- Remote MCP server: POST https://api.patchlabs.dev/mcp, JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP, stateless. Tools: rls_check {repo}, start_check {repo, email}, get_check {check_id}, list_apps and run_check {app_id} (these two need X-API-Key). Docs: https://patchlabs.dev/docs/mcp
- Health: GET https://api.patchlabs.dev/health returns {ok, db, worker_last_seen, queued}. Live status page: https://patchlabs.dev/status

## Signed receipts

Every finished check has a receipt signed with Ed25519: GET https://api.patchlabs.dev/receipts/<check id> returns {receipt, signature, key_id, algorithm}. The receipt holds check_id, repo, status, tables_leaking, lab_proof_passed, fix_sha256, finished_at, decisions and answers. Public key: GET https://api.patchlabs.dev/.well-known/patchlabs-receipt-key. Signed bytes: json.dumps(receipt, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")). Verify in the browser at https://patchlabs.dev/proof#verify or with the Python script at https://patchlabs.dev/security#receipts

## Security and privacy

- Reads: the public repo (code, migrations, git history), the verification file, the requester's email.
- Never: database passwords, service-role keys, production data, signed-in or API access to the live app, write access to the repo.
- Live probes: none from Lab or Code checks. Live posture (opt-in) loads only the public home page of a verified domain, like any visitor.
- Retention: lab database deleted after each check; working copy of the repo up to 30 days; reports, fixes and receipts until the user deletes them; account data until the account is deleted. Sign-in links 20 minutes; sessions 30 days; tokens and API keys stored only as hashes; IP addresses stored only as a salted hash.
- Where it runs: website on GitHub Pages; API and database in Microsoft Azure; checks on a worker machine operated by PatchLabs in London.
- Subprocessors: Anthropic (AI models), Microsoft Azure (hosting, database), GitHub (site hosting, repo reads), Spacemail by Spaceship (email).
- No cookies and no third-party analytics. localStorage holds only the session token and theme choice.
- Certifications: none held or claimed.
- Details: https://patchlabs.dev/security, https://patchlabs.dev/legal/privacy

## Limits

PatchLabs Lab tests database read access (Supabase/Postgres); PatchLabs Code checks keys, known risky code patterns and npm dependency versions. Code findings are pattern matches for a person to judge, not proofs. Live posture reads the HTTPS setup, certificate, headers and cookie flags of one public page; it is not a vulnerability scan. It is not a penetration test and does not test business logic. The lab is only as complete as the migrations in the repo: changes made only in the Supabase dashboard are invisible. A passing proof covers the tables tested, not the whole app. Public repos only for now. Checks run one at a time on one worker.
